properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-09-02: *"as agentic models get better and better, what will reflow2 do that allows it to keep its value? what are its traits that allow it to be enduring? I'm not saying let's cut the things a model can do, but let's start emphasizing and ensuring the things that a model doesn't or can't do well are done very well by reflow2."*

⭐ **THIS SESSION IS UNUSUALLY GOOD EVIDENCE, because it is a capable model failing about ten times in one day and being caught every time by something OUTSIDE itself.** Not a thought experiment — a log:

· Wrote prose contradicting code it had just written; came within one edit of adding a sixth instance of the class it was naming. Caught by a deliberate second pass.
· Ranked half-exact above declared WITH a confident comment explaining why, reproducing the exact reported bug. Caught by a test written from the reporter's words.
· Over-declared `GATED_ON`, laundering a modelling gap as a design choice. Caught by a test.
· Dropped BL-50's "modelled fit" wording. Caught by two tests written weeks earlier.
· Missed four pinned edge-type counts; fixed three by hand, CI caught the fourth — and that file's own comment PREDICTED the fourth would be missed.
· Forgot toolsnap regeneration twice. CI caught both.
· Reported tests green by counting PASSES while two were failing.
· Measured prevalence and inferred a cause from the rate, skipping the step that finds causes — caught only because Anthony pushed on an untested "what would refute this".
· Concluded a file had been "rewritten" from a failed prefix check when it was an extract.
· Pushed twice before running fmt/clippy.

**NONE OF THESE WERE REASONING FAILURES.** Every one is continuity, cross-checking or self-knowledge — and every one was caught by a record, a gate, a pinned count, a comment from a past session, or a person. That is the shape of the answer.

**THE SHARP FRAMING: A BETTER MODEL PRODUCES MORE PLAUSIBLE OUTPUT AND IS MORE PERSUASIVE TO ITSELF.** Its failure mode is not incoherence, it is a MORE CONFIDENT WRONG ANSWER. Today the model was most wrong exactly where it was most confident — the tier order shipped with a comment justifying it. So the demand for something that can say *no* to a fluent claim RISES with capability rather than falling.

CANDIDATE ENDURING TRAITS, none preferred and each stated so it can be argued with:

· **① MEMORY THAT OUTLIVES THE SESSION, THE AGENT AND THE PROJECT.** A cause root-caused on 2026-08-16 was re-diagnosed from scratch by three separate sessions across three projects, because none could see the others' record. Context windows growing does not fix this: a design outlives any session by construction, and consumers are separate graphs run by separate agents. ⚠️ Counter: if context becomes effectively unbounded AND shared across agents, this thins.

· **② REFUSAL TO ACCEPT THE AGENT'S OWN CLAIM.** `check_intent_authority` refused this model's own accepted Decisions because no human's name was on them — twice today. A better model does not fix that; it makes better-sounding unsupported claims. The value of "who said so, and on what evidence" grows with the fluency of the thing asserting.

· **③ CHEAP ADVERSARIAL CHECKS AT THE MOMENT OF WRITING.** Pinned counts, toolsnap goldens, the export lineage chain, `deny_unknown_fields`. Each is trivial and each caught something today. They work BECAUSE they do not reason — they cannot be talked round.

· **④ THE RECORD OF WHAT WAS REFUTED.** Two of the seven decisions settled today were refutations: the edge already existed; five of one fleet's asks had already shipped. **That is the single most expensive thing to lose**, because a capable model will cheerfully rebuild what exists and produce a good-looking PR doing it. Nothing in a model's training says "we already tried that and here is why it was wrong."

· **⑤ TELLING "NOBODY LOOKED" FROM "LOOKED AND FOUND NOTHING".** The `no_relation_note`, `swept.parked`, `rerun_owed`'s three-valued null, `expected_at_this_phase`. A model asked to summarise will fill silence with a plausible reading; only a record distinguishes an absence somebody judged from one nobody examined.

· **⑥ AUTHORITY SEPARATION — the human's word as a first-class, dated, attributable object.** As models get better the pull to let them decide gets stronger, and the value of being able to say WHOSE ruling this was, on what date, against what evidence, rises with it. `req:the-agent-never-authors-what-requires-accountable-sign-off` already reaches for this.

**WHAT HONESTLY ERODES, said plainly because pretending otherwise would make this useless:** the skills-as-workflow-teaching layer, gap PHRASING, and vocabulary routing ("which node type is this?"). A better model needs less of all three. They are scaffolding, not the thing that lasts — and that is fine, because Anthony did not ask to cut what a model can do.

⚠️ **THE STRONGEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT, and it is real:** a better model plus better harness could absorb ②③⑤ too — models can write their own tests, run their own gates, keep their own notes. The reply is that a check the same agent authors and runs shares its blind spots, and today's evidence is that the checks which caught this model were written by OTHER sessions, weeks earlier, for other reasons. But that is an argument about independence, not about model capability, and it would weaken if independence could be manufactured inside one agent. Nobody has tested that.

⚠️ NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any of this is what USERS actually value, as opposed to what this design can see itself doing. Every observation above is self-observation on reflow2's own development. The field reports say the load-bearing feature is the PROSE — which is not obviously any of the six.
properties.name: OPEN — as agentic models improve, what does reflow2 keep doing that they do badly? The candidate answer is that better models make MORE of the failure it catches, not less
properties.rationale:
Recorded as a question rather than a strategy because the evidence is one session of self-observation, and the one external signal available — what field reports actually praise — does not obviously match any of the six traits. That mismatch is the most interesting thing here and should not be smoothed over.

Worth capturing now rather than later because the evidence is perishable: a session where a capable model failed ten times in traceable ways, with each catch attributable, is a better basis for this argument than any amount of reasoning about it afterwards. Six weeks from now the log is gone and only the conclusion would remain.
